hypotheses.statement: Starting from orders_2026-10-14.csv, the column 'customer_id' was renamed to 'cust_id' (rename candidate score 0.89). The pipeline crashed because it expected the old header 'customer_id' but encountered 'cust_id' instead. No other columns changed format or were added/dropped.
hypotheses.falsification_check: Run column_by_file for 'cust_id' on data/current — if 'cust_id' appears in any file before 2026-10-14 (e.g., 2026-10-13), the rename hypothesis is disproved (it would be a new column, not a rename).
hypotheses.suggested_fix: Update the pipeline schema to accept both 'customer_id' and 'cust_id' as aliases, or add a header normalization step that renames 'cust_id' → 'customer_id' for files from 2026-10-14 onward before the main load.

verification.observations: column_by_file shows 'cust_id' first appears in orders_2026-10-14.csv (absent in all prior files 2026-10-08 through 2026-10-13), while 'customer_id' is present through 2026-10-13 and absent from 2026-10-14 onward. diff_schema confirms only a rename (customer_id → cust_id, score 0.89) with no other columns added, dropped, or format-changed. The falsification check did not disprove the hypothesis.
